Historical context from earlier work:

## Beads deep integration (lets-ji2, closed)
Audited all 10 commands for beads touchpoints. Before: only 4/10 used beads (start, end, status, finish). ## Beads best practices (lets-oeo, closed)
Added to rules-context.md:
- Epics are containers, NOT blockers - never add epic as dep for children
- bd dep only when task literally cannot start without another
- Parent-child uses --parent flag, NOT bd dep add
- Every task belongs to an epic - no orphans
- Epics are long-lived - don't close just because children done\n- Review epic structure every 5-10 sessions\n- AI tracks epics and suggests right parent when creating tasks

author: Dima Slep
text:
Historical context: Directed search vs exploration rule (lets-0nf.20, closed)

Insight from real usage: Claude optimizes for "I know where to look, I'll do it quickly myself", ignoring context window cost of sequential decision chains. Added rule to rules-context.md:

- Directed search (know WHAT and WHERE) -> use Glob/Grep/Read directly
- Exploration (synthesize, compare, discover patterns) -> use explorer sub-agent
- Escalate to agent when: 3+ read-then-decide rounds needed, comparing 3+ files, open-ended question

This is directly relevant to making explorer agent universal - it should be the default tool for any non-trivial codebase search.

author: Dima Slep
text:
## Decision 2026-03-01 - worktree location (CRITICAL)

**Chose:** .worktrees/ at project root
**Over:** .lets/worktrees/
**Because:** interactive worktree sessions need .lets/ access (for /lets:start, /lets:commit, etc). Symlink .lets/ -> main .lets/ inside worktree solves this. But if worktrees are INSIDE .lets/ - symlink creates circular path (.lets/worktrees/x/.lets -> .lets). Moving worktrees to .worktrees/ eliminates the cycle.

### Final architecture
- .worktrees/ at project root (gitignored)
- WorktreeCreate hook ALWAYS creates .lets/ symlink (harmless for agents, needed for interactive)
- WorktreeRemove hook removes symlink before cleanup
- .beads/redirect via bd worktree create (unchanged)

### Two use cases, one hook
- Agent isolation (isolation:worktree): uses code + beads, ignores .lets/ symlink
- Interactive sessions (claude --worktree): uses code + beads + .lets/ symlink for full LETS workflow

### Detection hint
- Agent worktree names start with "agent-" (from hook log)
- Interactive worktree names are user-specified or random words
- Can use this later to customize behavior if needed

author: Dima Slep
text:
## Research 2026-03-01 - /lets:start in worktree issues

### Issue 1: Branch creation conflict (CRITICAL)
/lets:start Step 6 tries to create feature/<task-id>-slug branch.
In worktree: already on worktree-<name> branch. Creating feature branch
on top works but is confusing - two branches for one worktree.

FIX OPTIONS:
A) Detect worktree, skip branch creation, use worktree branch as-is
B) Detect worktree, rename worktree branch to feature/<task-id>-slug
C) In worktree mode, /lets:start skips Step 6 entirely

Recommended: A - simplest. If in worktree, branch is already set.

DETECTION:
```bash
if [ "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" != ".git" ]; then
  echo "IN WORKTREE"
fi
```

### Issue 2: .session-start-ref race (CRITICAL)
Two parallel sessions overwrite same file.
/lets:end reads it to know which commits belong to this session.

FIX: Use branch name as key: .session-start-ref-<branch>
- Session 1 on feature/auth: .session-start-ref-feature-auth
- Session 2 on worktree-xyz: .session-start-ref-worktree-xyz
Changes needed: start.md (write), end.md (read)

### Issue 3: last-summary.md (ACCEPTABLE)
Last writer wins. Acceptable because:
- Dated archives exist (YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.md)
- last-summary.md is "most recent session", not "my session"
- /lets:start just uses it for context, not critical data

### Issue 4: project-root in worktree
session-start.sh injects worktree path as project-root.
This is CORRECT - git operations should use worktree path.
.lets/ accessible through symlink - transparent.

## Native worktree test 2026-03-01 - SUCCESS

### Decision: removed WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks
Our hooks (worktree-setup.sh, worktree-cleanup.sh) caused more harm than good:
- bd worktree create added .beads/redirect -> git saw 'changes' -> Claude Code skipped auto-cleanup
- .lets/ symlink wasn't gitignored properly (.lets/ with trailing slash doesn't match symlinks)
- WorktreeRemove never fired because Claude Code kept worktrees with 'changes'

### Native behavior (no hooks)
- Worktree created at .claude/worktrees/<name>/ (Claude Code default)
- git status: clean (no redirect, no symlink)
- Auto-cleanup on agent finish: WORKS
- CLAUDE.md accessible: YES
- pwd returns worktree path: YES

### What agents DON'T get without hooks
- No .beads/redirect (bd commands use stale JSONL snapshot)
- No .lets/ symlink (no LETS config access)
- But read-only agents don't need either of these

### Scripts preserved for future
- hooks/worktree-setup.sh - available for /lets:worktree (lets-hpi.1)
- hooks/worktree-cleanup.sh - available for interactive cleanup
- hooks/validate-readonly.sh - available for plugin-level sandboxing (lets-hpi.5)

author: Dima Slep
text:
## Insight: Beadbox 13-agent production (2026-03)

Beadbox runs 13 Claude Code agents in production. Sandboxing done via CLAUDE.md boundaries, not hooks:
- Each agent has identity + boundary section in CLAUDE.md
- 'eng2 can't close issues. qa1 doesn't write code.'
- Works at scale without technical enforcement

Validates our prompt-rules approach. Plugin-level hooks are nice-to-have, not critical.

author: Dima Slep
text:
## Insight: Beadbox uses tmux, not Agent Teams (2026-03)

Real-world 13-agent fleet uses:
- 13 separate claude sessions in tmux panes (NOT Agent Teams)
- gn/gp/ga tmux messaging tools for inter-agent communication
- beads (bd) for task coordination: bd update --claim --actor, bd comments add --author
- 'super' agent runs patrol loop every 5-10 min checking stalls

Key: tmux approach is more mature and controllable than Agent Teams.
Minimum viable: 'Two engineers and a QA agent, coordinated through beads.'

Consider: our lets-hpi.6 might pivot from Agent Teams to tmux-based multi-session.

author: Dima Slep
text:
## Insight: Beadbox multi-agent architecture (2026-03)

Beadbox uses 13 tmux panes, each a separate claude session with own CLAUDE.md.
QA agent has its own repo clone (not worktree) - tests pushed code, not working tree.

For /lets:worktree: interactive worktrees (tmux panes) are the proven pattern.
Consider supporting both:
- /lets:worktree create - for interactive parallel sessions
- tmux integration for multi-agent workflows later

text:
## Smoke test results 2026-03-02

### What works
- Guards (worktree check, active team, clean tree)
- TeamCreate + parallel Agent spawn (2 teammates, single message)
- Plan approval flow (plan_approval_request -> review -> approve)
- Implementation in worktrees (edit + commit)
- Task completion tracking via TaskList
- Shutdown + TeamDelete cleanup

### Key discovery: worktree auto-merge
isolation: worktree auto cherry-picks teammate commits onto the current branch when worktree is cleaned up. No separate branches survive after cleanup. This means:
- Trial merge section in team.md is unnecessary
- Branch discovery section is unnecessary
- Completion flow simplifies: just check git log for new commits

### Team config limitation
Only team-lead appears in ~/.claude/teams/{name}/config.json members array. Teammates don't register there. Can't use config for branch discovery (moot point since auto-merge).

### Idle notification spam
Completed teammates send repeated idle notifications (4+ from explorer-comment-1). Command should ignore idle from teammates whose task is already marked completed.

### Plan updates needed
1. Remove trial merge (R10.2-10.3) - replace with git log check
2. Remove branch discovery (R10.1) - not needed
3. Simplify completion: just verify commits landed on current branch
4. Add idle notification filtering for completed teammates
5. Output should show commits on current branch, not separate branches
